reading.body:
This campus represents 7.6 percent of Texas's published data center capacity, ranking fourth in the state at 36 MW, but most Texas facilities do not disclose their power or IT specifications, leaving the state's actual AI infrastructure largely unmapped.

CyrusOne San Antonio spans three facility codes across roughly 296,000 square feet, a footprint consistent with enterprise and cloud workloads rather than purpose-built AI training clusters. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 36 MW capacity suggests roughly 900 racks, though the operator publishes no tenant mix or actual utilization. The campus holds multiple compliance certifications including FISMA, HIPAA, and PCI DSS, which means it can host regulated government and healthcare data but also indicates it was designed for compliance-sensitive customers before the recent acceleration in AI compute demand.

Power infrastructure details are not published, leaving critical unknowns: whether the 36 MW reflects campus-wide power delivery or IT equipment limits only, what grid connection capacity exists, and whether backup generation can sustain continuous AI training loads. The certifications and footprint suggest this facility is not currently optimized for accelerator-dense clusters, and without visibility into actual tenant workloads or power delivery design, its role in AI scaling remains unclear. Texas ranks second nationally in disclosed data center capacity, yet only 19 facilities publish specifications against 133 mapped locations, meaning most of the state's power constraints and facility configurations for AI are invisible to planning and forecasting.
